annotation.method: Manually inspected saved passage text; labels assess substantive claims against cited passages, including scope when stated. Questions are retained for review but the existing judge API does not receive them. Unsupported maps to insufficient_evidence.
limitations: These are assistant annotations, not human-labelled gold data.
Known batch failure 23 is literally supported by a scope-stripped excerpt; it must not be counted as a judge failure to recognize contradiction.
Short fragment answers require question context, which the current judge API lacks. Calibration exposes this limitation.
Eight counterfactuals broaden negative coverage; the set is diagnostic, not representative of production prevalence.

A-5.2. To determine the maximum safe load-moment, the truck manufacturer normally rates the truck at a maximum load at a given distance from the front face of the forks. The specified distance from the front face of the forks to the line of action of the load is commonly called the load center. Because larger trucks normally handle loads that are physically larger, these vehicles have greater load centers. Trucks with a capacity of 30,000 pounds or less are normally rated at a given load weight at a 24-inch load center. Trucks with a capacity greater than 30,000 pounds are normally rated at a given load weight at a 36- or 48-inch load center. To safely operate the vehicle, the operator should always check the data plate to determine the maximum allowable weight at the rated load center.

A-5.3. Although the true load-moment distance is measured from the front wheels, this distance is greater than the distance from the front face of the forks.
